name: Custom Offense
subtitle: Scheme Kings · CFB 27
tagline: Read the safeties. Take the numbers.

about.headline: MY CUSTOM OFFENSE
copy: An offense I built from scratch in College Football 27, not copied from a real team. Four formations, the RPOs that read the safeties, the bunch motion, two man beaters and the vertical shots, and every call comes out of the Florida International playbook.

principles.title: READ THE SAFETIES
principles.blurb: Two high and they can only have five in the box, so we run it. As soon as we see single high, we work the seam balls.
principles.detail: RPO Alert WR Screens and Switch Seams out of the same look: two high, run the ball; single high, the seams. Flip back and forth between them.

principles.title: ONE MOTION, TWO PLAYS
principles.blurb: The toss and the flat use the same motion, and the jet runs the power and the read. They are not going to know if we are running or passing.
principles.detail: The bunch motion runs Motion Toss and Motion Spacing Z Flat, and the jet motion runs Jet HB Power and Jet RPO Read Slide.

principles.title: BEAT MAN EVERY SNAP
principles.blurb: Have at least two man beaters you trust. Curl Switch and PA Wave put four and five man beating routes on the field at once.
principles.detail: Curl Switch out of the stack and PA Wave off play action: five and four man beating routes, and both beat match too.

extras.text: Motion Spacing Z Flat is probably the best red zone play I have used all year.

playbook.title: RUN THE FIU PLAYBOOK
playbook.note: In College Football 27 this whole offense runs out of the FLORIDA INTERNATIONAL playbook. Normal Flex Snug, Bunch Str Nasty, Empty Trey Stack and Pistol Wing Flex Close all live inside it.

formations.name: Normal Flex Snug
formations.desc: Two receivers outside the hash on each side, snugged in. The defense has to match them, so the safeties tell you everything: two high and they only have five in the box, single high and the seams are open.
bullets: They squeeze inside: flip the screen

show.what: RPO Alert WR Screens. Two safeties back and two DBs outside, five players in the box. Six on five, hand it off.
Switch Seams. Single high, and the seams get open on both sides. Go away from the user.
PA Switch Sail. The wheel pulls the deep defender back and the corner breaks to the outside.

formations.name: Bunch Str Nasty
formations.desc: A tight bunch to the wide side with the motion coming down into it. The toss and Motion Spacing Z Flat share the motion, the bubble catches people inside, and the slot fade and the man beaters come out of the same look.
bullets: One motion, the toss or the flat
People get caught inside the bunch
The slot fade off the motion

show.what: Motion Toss. He cracks down and seals inside, two pullers lead, and we get the perimeter.
Motion Spacing Z Flat. The same motion. Against man his defender follows him inside and gets caught in the mess.
RPO Read Bubble. Less than three outside the bunch, drop it out right at the snap.

formations.name: Empty Trey Stack
formations.desc: Five out, a stack on one side and three on the other. The stack makes natural rubs against man, and the vertical routes put the deep defenders in a bind. Curl Switch and Fade Out both live here.
bullets: Fade Out: read the coverage pre-snap
Five out: get it out against the blitz

show.what: Curl Switch. The two defenders come into the same path off the stack, and the corner route breaks to the outside.
Fade Out. Single high, the wheel breaks to the outside, and the flat defender stays too shallow.
Post Wheel. The streak drives the deep defenders back and the Z post gets in behind the linebackers.

formations.name: Wing Flex Close
formations.desc: Pistol, with two receivers to the wide side and the tight ends to the short side. The jet motion pulls the defense one way for the read and the power, and the play action man beaters come off the same look.
bullets: The jet pulls players out of the box
The read option away from the motion
Play action and two crossers against man

show.what: Jet HB Power. He leaves the middle to the jet motion, and the puller is coming across to hit him.
Jet RPO Read Slide. We pull it, nobody is in the flat, and the tight end comes across the formation.
PA Wave. Two crossers in the middle of the field against man, and the tight end gets separation.

pillars.name: Base Offense
pillars.line: We use these to set everything up: nice runs and ways to move the football against whatever we face. Read the safeties and count the box, run it where they leave us the numbers, and take the seams when they go single high.

checks: Two high and five in the box: hand it off
Single high: the seams on Switch Seams
They follow the motion inside: Motion Spacing Z Flat breaks out

pillars.name: Man Beaters
pillars.line: Two of the better plays in this game, built to beat man coverage. We cannot control if the player we are facing runs man, so these also work if they are running zone, and both of them beat match.

checks: Two crossers in the middle of the field
The corner route off the stack
Get the ball out quick against the blitz

pillars.name: Vertical Pass Game
pillars.line: The vertical shots. Read the coverage pre-snap, get a gauge on what they like to run, and attack Cover 3, Cover 2 and match down the field.

checks: Single high: the wheel and the seam
Cover 2: the hole shot behind the flat defender
Match: the back of the stack on a post

pillars.name: Scheme Kings
pillars.line: The rest of the offense out of the same four formations, exclusive to Scheme Kings: the empty quick game and shots, the play action, the bubble read, Y Trail, and the jet series.

checks: Bench Corner: read the stack at the snap
Jet RPO Read Slide: almost a triple option

answers.name: Switch Seams
answers.label: Single High: the Seams
answers.why: When they jump down to single high, especially Cover 3, we can just absolutely brutalize them. It is like attacking the seams, but we do not have to worry about getting jammed. Whichever side the user goes to, go to the other side and drop it up the seam.
answers.do: Running back to the wide side of the field, no other adjustments.

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: The Seam Against Single High
answers.why: Look to the seam on the trips side. Wait till he clears: the hook defender usually gets pulled inside by our crosser, and he gets wide open up the seam.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: Smash Seam
answers.label: The Seam Against Single High
answers.why: In a single high look, Cover 3, we can also hit the seam ball as he goes up.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Middle receiver on the wide side on a streak. Back of the stack receiver on the short side on a streak.

answers.name: Switch Seams
answers.label: The Hole Shot Against Cover 2
answers.why: If they have a mid read, he usually opens up to the wide side, so drop it over the mid read. If the safety is splitting the difference, throw a hole shot on the short side up behind the corner.
answers.do: Running back to the wide side of the field, no other adjustments.

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: The Wheel Against Cover 2
answers.why: The streak pulls everyone inside, the wheel comes up behind the flat defender, and the flat defender does not turn and run in time. Drop it up over his head, a hole shot for 20 or 30 yards.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: Post Wheel
answers.label: Against Cover 2
answers.why: The streak drives everyone back. The linebacker stops at about ten yards, the user is rushing so he does not see it, and we drive it up over the linebackers' heads.
answers.do: Trips to the short side of the field. Inside receiver on the trips side on a streak.

answers.name: Curl Switch
answers.label: The Corner Route
answers.why: My favorite way to beat it is from the stack: the corner route. At the snap the two defenders come into the same path, which creates natural rubs. Even if they do not run into each other, it is one on one to the outside. If you get separation on the cut, fire it up.
answers.do: Stack to the wide side of the field. Front of the stack receiver on a corner route.

answers.name: PA Wave
answers.label: The Tight End Crosser
answers.why: Two crossers in the middle of the field, one tight end and one slot receiver. Hit the tight end as he comes across, make a guy miss and turn it into a massive pickup.
answers.do: Two receivers to the wide side of the field, the tight ends to the short side. Against man: block the running back. Against man: inside tight end on a drag. Against match: inside tight end on a corner route instead.

answers.name: Motion Spacing Z Flat
answers.label: The Tell Against Man
answers.why: If it is man you get a tell right away, because his man defender follows him all the way inside. He gets caught up in the mess and has a super hard time getting to the outside. Fire it in. Amazing versus press, because they cannot press that route.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field. Point man in the bunch on a streak. Backside receiver on a streak. Running back on a wheel.

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: Against Match: the Post
answers.why: Put the back of the stack receiver on a post instead. Against quarters the safety realizes late he has to guard the wheel, and the post breaks inside. Against Palms they switch jobs, and that is too hard of a cover as he breaks in on the post.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: PA Wave
answers.label: Against Match: the Corner
answers.why: Instead of putting the inside tight end on a drag, put him on a corner route. It turns into an outside shade look for the match defender on the deep post, with no help to the inside. The three vertical routes pull the other match defenders down, and we take the one on one shot up over the top.
answers.do: Two receivers to the wide side of the field, the tight ends to the short side. Against man: block the running back. Against man: inside tight end on a drag. Against match: inside tight end on a corner route instead.

answers.name: PA Switch Sail
answers.label: The Switch Release Against Match
answers.why: Against match, Cover 4 match, the players get crossed on the switch and are late reacting to the wheel. If he is late, they run into each other, and you can fire it up the field on the switch release.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field. Back of the stack receiver on the short side on a post sit (he is usually on a curl). Optional: running back on a swing to the short side.

threats.q: How do I attack zero man?
threats.avoid: Careful with Curl Switch: five players are out on routes, so if they are blitzing you have to get the ball out quick

answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field. Point man in the bunch on a streak. Backside receiver on a streak. Running back on a wheel.

answers.name: PA Wave
answers.label: The Drag
answers.why: Right off the snap, if we do not like the deeper options, we have the drag coming from the tight end. Drop it out to him.
answers.do: Two receivers to the wide side of the field, the tight ends to the short side. Against man: block the running back. Against man: inside tight end on a drag. Against match: inside tight end on a corner route instead.

threats.q: How do I beat two safeties deep?

answers.name: RPO Alert WR Screens
answers.label: Hand It Off
answers.why: As soon as we see that, hand it off. A double team, get to the second level, and with the safeties back we have so much room to operate. Eight to ten yards basically every single time.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field (it really does not matter on this play).

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: The Inside Seam Against Cover 2
answers.why: The deep over brings the hooks inside, especially with no middle read, and the deep defenders get pulled outside by the streaks. The inside seam from our middle player gets wide open down the middle of the field.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.do: Running back to the wide side of the field, no other adjustments.

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: The Wheel Against Cover 3
answers.why: Single high, the wheel route breaks to the outside. If the flat defender stays inside or stays too shallow, throw the wheel as he turns up field.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: Smash Seam

threats.name: Hit an explosive play
threats.q: How do I hit an explosive play?

answers.name: Post Wheel
answers.label: The Z Post
answers.why: I like to work the short side first. The streak drives the deep defenders back, and if we have time in the pocket and it is zone, wait for the Z post to clear into the middle of the field. He gets 15, 20 yards in behind the linebackers, drop it in over the top for a 40 yard gain.
answers.do: Trips to the short side of the field. Inside receiver on the trips side on a streak.

answers.name: Fade Out
answers.label: The Inside Seam Against Cover 2
answers.why: The deep over brings the hooks inside, especially with no middle read, and the deep defenders get pulled outside by the streaks. The inside seam from our middle player gets wide open down the middle of the field.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak. Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post.

answers.name: Motion Toss
answers.label: Make a Guy Miss
answers.why: Hat on a hat, get to the edge, make a guy miss in the open field. I have hit some really big runs to the outside with it, a 67 yard run, a 30 yard gain.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field.

threats.name: Move the chains
threats.q: How do I move the chains?

answers.name: RPO Alert WR Screens
answers.label: Hand It Off
answers.why: As soon as we see that, hand it off. A double team, get to the second level, and with the safeties back we have so much room to operate. Eight to ten yards basically every single time.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field (it really does not matter on this play).

answers.name: Motion Spacing Z Flat
answers.label: Against Zone: a Flat Route
answers.why: Against zone the corner does not come down inside. He might walk in a step or two, but he stays outside in his zone. Treat it like a flat route: if we see green grass on the outside, throw it.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field. Point man in the bunch on a streak. Backside receiver on a streak. Running back on a wheel.

answers.name: Bench Corner
answers.label: The Shallow Seam
answers.why: I call it throwing up the shallow seam, about seven and eight yards as he cuts upfield. At the snap they all jump outside, which you see a ton in Cover 3, and as long as the linebacker stays inside and does not jump over this route, throw it up as soon as he cuts upfield. It works really well on the goal line too.
answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak.

threats.name: Get a playmaker in space
threats.q: How do I get a playmaker in space?

answers.name: RPO Read Bubble
answers.label: The Numbers Advantage
answers.why: Our eyes are out here right away. If they have less than three people outside, right at the snap drop it out. Three on two, let those guys block and get it in our playmaker's hands.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field.

answers.name: RPO Alert WR Screens
answers.label: They Squeeze Inside: Flip It Out
answers.why: When they keep two safeties back but start to squeeze inside on the run, we have a two on one on the outside. It is just a numbers game. Flip it out to the perimeter and get it into a playmaker's hands.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field (it really does not matter on this play).

answers.name: PA Switch Sail
answers.label: The Running Back Swing
answers.why: If we are getting pressure in our face or everybody is dropping back onto the post sit and the crosser, throw the swing, make some guys miss and make a play in the open field.
answers.do: Running back to the short side of the field. Back of the stack receiver on the short side on a post sit (he is usually on a curl). Optional: running back on a swing to the short side.

threats.name: Get the QB involved
threats.q: How do I get the quarterback involved?

answers.name: RPO Read Bubble
answers.label: The Read Crashes: Pull It
answers.why: If it is three on three, we do not need to throw it. But the read defender crashes, so we pull it. All these guys get pulled outside to the bubble, and there is an absolutely massive hole for the QB run.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field.

answers.name: Jet RPO Read Slide
answers.label: Keep It With the QB
answers.why: If everyone gets pulled to the tight end, we can also keep it with our QB. On the goal line the read crashes, nobody is out there, so keep it and get into the end zone.
answers.do: Two receiver side to the wide side of the field. Inside receiver on the two receiver side on a streak (on the goal line or against man, a slant).

answers.label: Two Pullers
answers.why: He cracks down and seals inside, and we get two pullers coming out leading. Seal everyone inside and get the perimeter.

threats.name: Third and short
threats.q: What do I call on third and short?

answers.name: Motion Spacing Z Flat
answers.label: The Motion Out Route
answers.why: The best route and the go to route here is this motion in, break back out route. He starts out, motions in just like the toss, then he arrows to the flat.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field. Point man in the bunch on a streak. Backside receiver on a streak. Running back on a wheel.

answers.name: RPO Read Bubble
answers.label: Hand It Off
answers.why: If you do not like the look outside, hand it off to the running back going away from the flow of the RPO. Third and two, and we pick up twelve yards.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field.

answers.name: Jet HB Power
answers.label: A Quick Hitter Up the Gut
answers.why: The motion comes across, the user steps out, and it is a quick hitter right up the gut. Get downhill right away. We are 15 yards upfield before they even realize we did not hand it off to the jet.
answers.do: No setup.

threats.name: Third and long
threats.q: What do I call on third and long?

answers.name: Smash Seam
answers.label: The Outside Breaking Corner
answers.why: A vertical shot play, really good on third and long against drop zone, Cover 3, Cover 2, Cover 4 drop. The corner route breaks outside and then breaks up, the streak pulls everyone back, the flat defenders get to about 15 to 20 yards, and we drop it up over his head. Pass it up and away along the sideline.

answers.label: The Slant
answers.why: Against man the really sharp breaking slant can get open. Against zone the flat defender stays too shallow, the streak pulls everyone back, and there is a pocket in behind the flat defender. It almost works like a slant that turns into a crosser.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field. Point man in the bunch on a streak. Backside receiver on a streak. Running back on a wheel.

answers.name: Motion Spacing Z Flat
answers.label: The Running Back Wheel
answers.why: When he shoots outside, the flat defender runs with him. The slant and the streak pull back the deep defenders and pull the linebackers inside, and it leaves a wicked pocket for the wheel to shoot up in, right into the end zone.
answers.do: Bunch to the wide side of the field. Point man in the bunch on a streak. Backside receiver on a streak. Running back on a wheel.

answers.do: Trips to the wide side of the field. Middle receiver on the wide side on a streak. Back of the stack receiver on the short side on a streak.

home.pitch: The offense I built from scratch in College Football 27: the RPOs that read the safeties, the bunch motion, two man beaters and the vertical shots. All of it out of the Florida International playbook.

book.note: every formation and every call on the sheet lives inside it

plays.name: RPO Alert WR Screens

reads.label: Look at the Safeties
reads.text: The key with this play is we are looking at our safeties. It is an amazing run to utilize when they are keeping their safeties back, when they are playing two high safeties.

reads.label: Five in the Box
reads.text: We have two receivers outside the hash on each side. If they keep two safeties back and two DBs outside to match our receivers, they can only have five players in the box. Five offensive linemen plus our running back: we outnumber them six on five.

reads.label: Hand It Off
reads.text: As soon as we see that, hand it off. A double team, get to the second level, and with the safeties back we have so much room to operate. Eight to ten yards basically every single time.

reads.label: They Squeeze Inside: Flip It Out
reads.text: When they keep two safeties back but start to squeeze inside on the run, we have a two on one on the outside. It is just a numbers game. Flip it out to the perimeter and get it into a playmaker's hands.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field (it really does not matter on this play)
plays.whenToUse: The first call against a new opponent. Two high safeties and two DBs over our receivers leaves five in the box, so hand it off. They squeeze inside, flip the screen out. They go single high, Switch Seams is in your audibles, so flip back and forth between them.

plays.name: Switch Seams

reads.label: Single High: the Seams
reads.text: When they jump down to single high, especially Cover 3, we can just absolutely brutalize them. It is like attacking the seams, but we do not have to worry about getting jammed. Whichever side the user goes to, go to the other side and drop it up the seam.

reads.label: They Rotate to Cover 2
reads.text: If they start single high and rotate, now it is Cover 2. We can still attack the middle of the field, we just have to wait till he clears in behind the vert hook.

reads.label: The Hole Shot Against Cover 2
reads.text: If they have a mid read, he usually opens up to the wide side, so drop it over the mid read. If the safety is splitting the difference, throw a hole shot on the short side up behind the corner.

reads.label: The Hard Flat
reads.text: You can also attack the wide side against Cover 2, but only if they are playing a hard flat. He is not getting back at all, and that opens up a big hole shot on the wide side.

reads.label: They Switch to Man
reads.text: We do not want to call it if we think they are in man, but if they switch it up on us, the running back is on an option route. Against zone he sits down, against man he breaks in or out. Fire it in and let him make a play in the open field.

adjustments: Running back to the wide side of the field, no other adjustments
plays.whenToUse: The other half of the two play combo with RPO Alert WR Screens. Two high, run the ball. As soon as we see single high, work those seam balls as they cut up the field. Two seams on the field, go away from the user.

plays.name: Motion Toss

reads.label: The Auto Motion
reads.text: Bunch to the wide side, and we get this auto motion down on this play. The receiver auto motions down and cracks inside.

reads.label: Same Motion, Two Plays
reads.text: This and Motion Spacing Z Flat use the same motion, so they are not going to know if we are running to the outside or passing. They work really well off each other.

reads.label: Two Pullers
reads.text: He cracks down and seals inside, and we get two pullers coming out leading. Seal everyone inside and get the perimeter.

reads.label: Make a Guy Miss
reads.text: Hat on a hat, get to the edge, make a guy miss in the open field. I have hit some really big runs to the outside with it, a 67 yard run, a 30 yard gain.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The toss off the bunch motion. A lot of the time I do not find these tosses very good, but the blocking on this one works a lot better: the crack inside, two pullers, and the perimeter.

plays.name: Motion Spacing Z Flat

reads.label: The Motion Out Route
reads.text: The best route and the go to route here is this motion in, break back out route. He starts out, motions in just like the toss, then he arrows to the flat.

reads.label: The Tell Against Man
reads.text: If it is man you get a tell right away, because his man defender follows him all the way inside. He gets caught up in the mess and has a super hard time getting to the outside. Fire it in. Amazing versus press, because they cannot press that route.

reads.label: Against Zone: a Flat Route
reads.text: Against zone the corner does not come down inside. He might walk in a step or two, but he stays outside in his zone. Treat it like a flat route: if we see green grass on the outside, throw it.

reads.label: The Running Back Wheel
reads.text: When he shoots outside, the flat defender runs with him. The slant and the streak pull back the deep defenders and pull the linebackers inside, and it leaves a wicked pocket for the wheel to shoot up in, right into the end zone.

reads.label: The Slant
reads.text: Against man the really sharp breaking slant can get open. Against zone the flat defender stays too shallow, the streak pulls everyone back, and there is a pocket in behind the flat defender. It almost works like a slant that turns into a crosser.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
Point man in the bunch on a streak
Backside receiver on a streak
Running back on a wheel
plays.whenToUse: One of the best plays I have used all year, and probably the best red zone play. Amazing on third and short, amazing versus man, amazing on the goal line. It beats every coverage, you just have to read it out.

plays.name: PA Wave

reads.label: Quick Separation
reads.text: Four really good man beaters on the field at once. As you drop back, we are just looking for who is getting separation quickly.

reads.label: The Tight End Crosser
reads.text: Two crossers in the middle of the field, one tight end and one slot receiver. Hit the tight end as he comes across, make a guy miss and turn it into a massive pickup.

reads.label: The Receiver Crosser
reads.text: We see the tight end crosser coming, but then the receiver crosser comes in behind him. Hit the receiver crosser as he separates.

reads.label: The Deep Post
reads.text: This route gets an outside release, then gets up field. If they do not have safety help in the middle of the field, it turns into a one on one with his man coverage player. As he breaks inside he separates, and we can bomb it over the top.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: Right off the snap, if we do not like the deeper options, we have the drag coming from the tight end. Drop it out to him.

reads.label: Against Match: the Corner
reads.text: Instead of putting the inside tight end on a drag, put him on a corner route. It turns into an outside shade look for the match defender on the deep post, with no help to the inside. The three vertical routes pull the other match defenders down, and we take the one on one shot up over the top.

adjustments: Two receivers to the wide side of the field, the tight ends to the short side
Against man: block the running back
Against man: inside tight end on a drag
Against match: inside tight end on a corner route instead
plays.whenToUse: One of our two good man beaters: two crossers, the deep post and the drag. If they keep the safeties back and still run man, the underneath options are there. Put the inside tight end on a corner and it beats match too.

plays.name: Curl Switch

reads.label: The Corner Route
reads.text: My favorite way to beat it is from the stack: the corner route. At the snap the two defenders come into the same path, which creates natural rubs. Even if they do not run into each other, it is one on one to the outside. If you get separation on the cut, fire it up.

reads.label: The Back of the Stack Post
reads.text: If we do not have a safety over the top, look to the back of the stack post. It is a one on one, his defender is usually in an outside shade, and as he breaks inside that naturally gives you separation. Go up over the top.

reads.label: The Tight End Shallow
reads.text: If we do not like the look of the stack, I am usually looking to the tight end first. He comes inside and gets really good separation as he cuts across the field.

reads.label: The Whip and the Dig
reads.text: The whip breaks out and the dig breaks up over the top. If we see separation on the whip, fire it in, or wait for the dig to attack the middle of the field as the Z post goes up over the top.

adjustments: Stack to the wide side of the field
Front of the stack receiver on a corner route
plays.whenToUse: A very good man play with five ways to beat man on the field at once. You do have to be cautious if they are blitzing, five players are out on routes, so get the ball out quick.

plays.name: Fade Out

reads.label: The Wheel Against Cover 3
reads.text: Single high, the wheel route breaks to the outside. If the flat defender stays inside or stays too shallow, throw the wheel as he turns up field.

reads.label: The Wheel Against Cover 2
reads.text: The streak pulls everyone inside, the wheel comes up behind the flat defender, and the flat defender does not turn and run in time. Drop it up over his head, a hole shot for 20 or 30 yards.

reads.label: The Seam Against Single High
reads.text: Look to the seam on the trips side. Wait till he clears: the hook defender usually gets pulled inside by our crosser, and he gets wide open up the seam.

reads.label: The Inside Seam Against Cover 2
reads.text: The deep over brings the hooks inside, especially with no middle read, and the deep defenders get pulled outside by the streaks. The inside seam from our middle player gets wide open down the middle of the field.

reads.label: The Deep Cross
reads.text: Cover 3 or Cover 2, we are just looking at whether the linebackers play too shallow. The user jumps over, the linebacker stays shallow, and it opens up the middle of the field for the deep over.

reads.label: Against Match: the Post
reads.text: Put the back of the stack receiver on a post instead. Against quarters the safety realizes late he has to guard the wheel, and the post breaks inside. Against Palms they switch jobs, and that is too hard of a cover as he breaks in on the post.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Against Cover 3 or Cover 2: back of the stack receiver on a streak
Against match: back of the stack receiver on a post
plays.whenToUse: A lot of this is reading coverage pre-snap. Get an idea of what your opponent likes to run: Cover 3, Cover 2 or match, and we know how we want to attack them. One of the best vertical passing plays you will use all year.

plays.name: Mtn China Wheel

reads.label: The Slot Fade
reads.text: The key route is the slot fade that motions over from the tight end. The streak pulls the deep defender back and holds him inside, and the flat defenders will not ride him. They usually stop at ten yards, so drop it up over their heads as he fades to the back pylon.

reads.label: Back Shoulder It
reads.text: The slot fade just fades right out to the sideline, the streak pulls this guy back, and there is a nice hole where you can back shoulder it up along the sideline. A free 20, 25 yards whenever you want it.

reads.label: The Dig
reads.text: If the slot fade is not there, go to the middle of the field. If the linebackers are staying shallow on the return route, wait for the dig and hit it as he breaks in over the middle.

reads.label: The Return Route
reads.text: If the linebacker stays deep on the dig, throw the return route underneath as he comes in and pick up a first down.

reads.label: The Running Back in the Flat
reads.text: The checkdown. If the user leaves the play, the running back is in the flat. Get it out to him and let him make a play with the ball in his hands.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
Solo receiver on a streak
Point man in the bunch on a return route
plays.whenToUse: The slot fade off the motion: the streak holds the deep defender, the flat defenders stop at ten, and it drops in up along the sideline or to the back pylon in the high red zone.

plays.name: Post Wheel

reads.label: The Z Post
reads.text: I like to work the short side first. The streak drives the deep defenders back, and if we have time in the pocket and it is zone, wait for the Z post to clear into the middle of the field. He gets 15, 20 yards in behind the linebackers, drop it in over the top for a 40 yard gain.

reads.label: Against Cover 2
reads.text: The streak drives everyone back. The linebacker stops at about ten yards, the user is rushing so he does not see it, and we drive it up over the linebackers' heads.

reads.label: The Wheel Behind the Flat
reads.text: The Z post and the streak pull back the deep defenders. Once the flat on the short side settles, throw the wheel up behind him. Back shoulder it up along the sideline.

reads.label: The Curl
reads.text: If we are getting pressure or the user is taking away the Z post, look to the middle of the field. If the linebackers stay inside on the drag and the curl is open, throw the curl as he sits down in the zone.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: If everybody stays back on all our vertical routes, or it is man and everything is covered down the field, check it down to the drag underneath.

adjustments: Trips to the short side of the field
Inside receiver on the trips side on a streak
plays.whenToUse: Three routes that interact on the short side: the streak drives the deep defenders back, the Z post and the wheel go behind them. The drag and the curl attack the middle.

plays.name: Smash Seam

reads.label: The Outside Breaking Corner
reads.text: A vertical shot play, really good on third and long against drop zone, Cover 3, Cover 2, Cover 4 drop. The corner route breaks outside and then breaks up, the streak pulls everyone back, the flat defenders get to about 15 to 20 yards, and we drop it up over his head. Pass it up and away along the sideline.

reads.label: On the Goal Line
reads.text: Look at the flat defender. He is getting 15 yards, 20 yards. If he keeps backpedaling, throw it to the back pylon of the end zone.

reads.label: The Deep Over
reads.text: If they are running some sort of match or man and the corner route is taken away, look to the deep over. The two vertical routes on the short side pull everyone back, and we fire in the deep over as he breaks in over the top.

reads.label: The Seam Against Single High
reads.text: In a single high look, Cover 3, we can also hit the seam ball as he goes up.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: If all three vertical routes are covered, we have the really shallow cross breaking in underneath over the middle. Put it in a playmaker's hands.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Middle receiver on the wide side on a streak
Back of the stack receiver on the short side on a streak
plays.whenToUse: The third and long shot: the outside breaking corner gets super deep down the field behind the flat defenders, with the deep over, the seam and the shallow cross behind it.

plays.name: Bench Corner

reads.label: Eyes on the Stack
reads.text: The place I always look first is the stack side: the inside breaking C route and the quick out, run from a stack alignment. It is a really hard cover for the DBs.

reads.label: The Shallow Seam
reads.text: I call it throwing up the shallow seam, about seven and eight yards as he cuts upfield. At the snap they all jump outside, which you see a ton in Cover 3, and as long as the linebacker stays inside and does not jump over this route, throw it up as soon as he cuts upfield. It works really well on the goal line too.

reads.label: The Out Route
reads.text: It is just the opposite. If this player stays in over the shallow seam and this one is in off coverage, our eyes are already there: throw the out route.

reads.label: The Wide Side
reads.text: If the user jumps over to take the stack away, work the wide side: the clear out route, and the corner from our inside slot receiver as he breaks to the outside. If the flat defender stays shallow, throw it.

reads.label: The C Route Later
reads.text: If the corner is taken, come back to the C route. Cover 2 and the flat defender bites down, throw it as a hole shot in between the safety and the corner. Man and you get separation, throw it as he breaks to the outside.

reads.label: The Shallow In Cut
reads.text: The checkdown. If the shallow seam is taken and the out route is taken, the shallow in cut breaks over the middle of the field.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak
plays.whenToUse: A zone reading quick game call off the stack: they jump out, the shallow seam; they stay in, the out route. Really nice in the red zone and on the goal line too. I do not really call this against man.

plays.name: PA Switch Sail

reads.label: The Corner Behind the Clear Out
reads.text: The first place I look is the switch release on the wide side: really just a clear out route with the C route breaking to the outside. Read the flat defender. Against Cover 2 match the wheel pulls back the deep defender, and the corner route is wide open as he breaks to the outside.

reads.label: The Switch Release Against Match
reads.text: Against match, Cover 4 match, the players get crossed on the switch and are late reacting to the wheel. If he is late, they run into each other, and you can fire it up the field on the switch release.

reads.label: The Deep Crosser
reads.text: If they match it well, or the zone drops are set deep, our eyes come to the short side. Wait till the deep crosser clears the linebacker and drop it in, kind of behind his ear.

reads.label: The Post Sit
reads.text: The crosser is taken by the linebacker and the user, the running back swing is taken, the flat bites down. Now the post sits down in this hole, and we drop it in on the backside.

reads.label: The Running Back Swing
reads.text: If we are getting pressure in our face or everybody is dropping back onto the post sit and the crosser, throw the swing, make some guys miss and make a play in the open field.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field
Back of the stack receiver on the short side on a post sit (he is usually on a curl)
Optional: running back on a swing to the short side
plays.whenToUse: If you are struggling with anything like Cover 2 match, this is going to be very good for you: the clear out and the corner on the wide side, then the deep crosser, the post sit and the swing.

plays.name: RPO Read Bubble

reads.label: Eyes on the Bubble
reads.text: A very good bubble screen. Because of the tight alignment, most of the time people get caught inside, and one of the players who should be playing out on the bubble becomes the read defender. He has to play either the run or the pass, he cannot go out on the screen.

reads.label: The Numbers Advantage
reads.text: Our eyes are out here right away. If they have less than three people outside, right at the snap drop it out. Three on two, let those guys block and get it in our playmaker's hands.

reads.label: The Read Crashes: Pull It
reads.text: If it is three on three, we do not need to throw it. But the read defender crashes, so we pull it. All these guys get pulled outside to the bubble, and there is an absolutely massive hole for the QB run.

reads.label: Go to the Outside
reads.text: If you go to the outside, these guys actually block for you on your QB run. Get up field, turn the corner, a ten, eleven yard gain.

reads.label: Hand It Off
reads.text: If you do not like the look outside, hand it off to the running back going away from the flow of the RPO. Third and two, and we pick up twelve yards.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: A read option with a bubble built in. Count the bubble side first: less than three out there, throw it. Even, read the read defender: he crashes, pull it. Do not like the outside, hand it off away from the flow.

plays.name: Y Trail

reads.label: The Corner Route Against Man
reads.text: Four really good man beaters: the drag across the bunch, the backside post, the trail route from the tight end, and the corner route from the middle player in the bunch. He gets upfield, breaks outside with about four yards of separation, and we fire it up over the top.

reads.label: Against Zone: Motion Him Out
reads.text: If you think they are running zone, or you are not sure, motion the outside player on the bunch out and put him on a streak. He becomes a clear out for the corner. The flat defender bites down, and we throw the corner up over the top.

reads.label: The Trail Route
reads.text: Against match, the match got confused and the trail route gets wide open going against the flow. If the linebackers play way back on the post, throw the trail underneath. Against man he gets really good separation.

reads.label: The Post
reads.text: If they do not have deep safety help, the post does very, very good against man. Really nice separation.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: The drag coming across the bunch is super tough to cover, with the speed coming across the middle of the field. Fire it in.

reads.label: The Running Back Swing
reads.text: The flat defender gets back underneath our corner route, so we have the running back swing in the flat. Get it out to him and pick up the first down.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
Against man: outside receiver on the wide side on the drag, and keep the running back on a swing or block him
Against zone or not sure: motion the outside receiver on the bunch out and put him on a streak
plays.whenToUse: Two ways to set it up. Against man, four man beaters on the field. Against zone, or if you are not sure, motion the outside player out on a streak and it clears out for the corner, with three man beaters still on the field.

plays.name: Jet RPO Read Slide

reads.label: The Jet Motion
reads.text: The jet motion goes to the short side of the field, and it can pull the user and the linebackers away from the flow. Then it is a read option on the wide side, away from the motion.

reads.label: The Read Defender: Pull It
reads.text: If the read defender gets pulled out, or he crashes, we just pull the football and get out.

reads.label: The Tight End in the Flat
reads.text: The tight end comes across the formation at the snap, the opposite way of the jet motion, and goes out to the flat. When we pull it, if nobody is in the flat, drop it into him. It almost becomes a triple option. 27 yards, down to the one yard line.

reads.label: Keep It With the QB
reads.text: If everyone gets pulled to the tight end, we can also keep it with our QB. On the goal line the read crashes, nobody is out there, so keep it and get into the end zone.

reads.label: The Backside Slant or the Seam
reads.text: On the goal line, or if you think it might be man, put the inside receiver on a slant. If everyone bites inside on the run, fire in the backside slant. Leave him on a streak and if the linebackers all bite inside, there is an opening up the seam.

adjustments: Two receiver side to the wide side of the field
Inside receiver on the two receiver side on a streak (on the goal line or against man, a slant)
plays.whenToUse: A read option with the jet motion pulling the defense the other way and the tight end sliding out to the flat behind it: hand it off, pull it, or throw it to the tight end. The same jet motion as Jet HB Power.

plays.name: Jet HB Power

reads.label: Pull Them Out of the Box
reads.text: The jet motion coming across does a good job of pulling guys out of the box. Then we have a really quick hitting power play up the middle of the field.

reads.label: Hit by Our Puller
reads.text: Look at this player: he leaves the middle to the jet motion, and that sets him up to be hit by our puller as he comes across. The receiver gets to the second level.

reads.label: A Quick Hitter Up the Gut
reads.text: The motion comes across, the user steps out, and it is a quick hitter right up the gut. Get downhill right away. We are 15 yards upfield before they even realize we did not hand it off to the jet.

plays.whenToUse: The run off the jet motion: the motion pulls players out of the middle and the back hits it right up the gut behind the puller. Jet Pass Fake Zone, the jet touch pass, is another wrinkle you can throw in to set it up.

plays.name: PA Flood

reads.label: The Deep Out
reads.text: A hard play action fake at the start. The number one route is the deep out from our receiver on the two receiver side, with the wheel going up as a clear out. If the flat defender stays shallow, let the clear out pull them back and throw it as he breaks.

reads.label: Against Match
reads.text: This also works really good against match coverage. It turns into a one on one route against the safety, and he has no help. Nice separation as he breaks out, fire it in.

reads.label: The Dig or the Post
reads.text: Judge how their linebackers are playing after the play action. If they are getting depth, the post works better: pass lead it back away from the safety. If they are staying shallow, keep it on the dig and throw it up over the top of them.

reads.label: The Running Back in the Flat
reads.text: We fake to the running back and he goes out in the flat. If everyone is playing back underneath our vertical options, check it down and let him make a play in the open field.

adjustments: Two receiver side to the wide side of the field
Optional: outside tight end on a post instead of the deep dig
plays.whenToUse: Play action flood: a hard fake, the wheel clears out, the deep out comes in behind it, and the dig or the post goes over the linebackers.
